summary: One of six Prince Albert National Park fire towers, built 1940 and decommissioned in 2001; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Decommissioned in 2001 with the park's other fire towers. No source read says whether the Boundary tower still stands.

notes_for_editor: The museum page is the only source for the 1940 date and the 2001 decommissioning. The Firetowers of Saskatchewan table gives Boundary's position but leaves its height and construction year blank; its photos under the park towers are dated March 21, 1991 with no stated meaning, so they are not used. The museum's cupola, cabin and crew details describe the park's towers in general and are not tied to Boundary. The candidate notes cite the same museum for 2001. A federal listing for a Sanctuary Fire Tower Cabin turned up in search; it is a different structure and is not used. No source read says whether the Boundary tower still stands or what is at the site. Fact-check 2026-10-20: the 53-57.0167 X 106-44.5000 position sits under a BOUNDARY entry in the general Saskatchewan list, while the BOUNDARY TOWER entry under P.A. NATIONAL PARK TOWERS gives no location; the story treats them as one tower, which the page does not state outright. A search of the Parks Canada page found no mention of Boundary.
